euronews.title: Tension rises in Ceuta: two migrant children stabbed and bacteria-contaminated beach
euronews.description: Two migrant children were stabbed in a knife attack in Ceuta, while health authorities have found high levels of bacteria in the water at Trampolín beach, near a migrant camp. The migration crisis is forcing some people to sleep in garages, vehicles and on rooftops.

euronews.title: US suspends consular services in Brazil as Lula and Bolsonaro fight for election
euronews.description: President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and rival Flavio Bolsonaro are pulling no punches in a last-ditch effort to win voters ahead of Sunday's election in Brazil, where the US and Australia suspended consular services Friday over security concerns.

euronews.title: Sánchez begins reflection on early election as protesters call for general strike
euronews.description: Spanish Prime Minister will decide this weekend whether to call early elections after his two housing decrees were rejected, as housing activists prepare fresh protests and consider a general strike as the next step.

euronews.title: Russia 'tearing Kyiv apart', mayor says, as strikes paralyse traffic
euronews.description: Russian attacks on key infrastructure were "tearing Kyiv apart", the city's mayor said Friday, as strikes on a bridge linking the capital's east and west brought traffic to a standstill.

euronews.title: Debt-saddled Argentina pitches 'golden passport' scheme to woo wealthy foreigners
euronews.description: Argentina on Friday announced plans to offer citizenship to wealthy foreigners in exchange for cash contributions or investments in government bonds, as libertarian President Javier Milei seeks new sources of dollars for the debt-burdened nation.

euronews.title: DR Congo Ebola outbreak killed more than 4,000: official figures
euronews.description: The worst ever Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has now killed more than 4,000 people out of more than 8,000 confirmed cases, Congolese officials said on Friday.

euronews.title: French students clash with police as school protests spread nationwide
euronews.description: Footage shows pupils in Paris, Toulouse and Lille clashing with police as they demand better school resources, warning protests will continue nationwide.

euronews.title: The solar system will fall apart far sooner than anyone thought, scientists say
euronews.description: Earth will be long gone by then, but new research shows the outer planets will be thrown out too, and a billion times earlier than expected, according to astrophysics research.

euronews.title: G7 agrees 100 million-barrel emergency oil release amid US pressure over diesel
euronews.description: The G7, led by France, announced the release of 100 million barrels of diesel and crude oil after Trump threatened a ban of diesel exports.

euronews.title: Putin says all weapons 'on agenda' if Russia's Kaliningrad attacked
euronews.description: Russia would consider using "all types of weapons" if its exclave of Kaliningrad was attacked, Russian President Vladimir Putin said Thursday, while insisting that Moscow had "no intention of attacking anyone."

euronews.title: Assisi marks 800 years since St Francis's death and remains a symbol of peace and dialogue
euronews.description: Today we honour Saint Francis, symbol of peace and diplomacy. On the 800th anniversary of his death, Euronews revisits his meeting with the sultan of Egypt and what this charismatic figure still has to teach us.

euronews.title: Beyond K-pop and cinema: Major Korean exhibition brings centuries of art and belief to London
euronews.description: The exhibition includes 10 national treasures and official Korean designations recognising their cultural importance, with most exhibits drawn from the collection of late Samsung billionaire Lee Kun-Hee.

euronews.title: 5,000 drones turn China’s night sky into a giant light show
euronews.description: A fleet of 5,000 drones forms fighter jets, robots, planes and horses over Nanchang as China marks National Day with a spectacular night show.

euronews.title: Spanish Congress rejects housing laws despite Sánchez's warning: 'They'll be judged sooner than they think'
euronews.description: Spanish Congress rejects two key housing measures aimed at quelling public uproar over housing affordability. The bills' rejection after last-minute talks leaves Pedro Sánchez's government without two key housing measures and exposes its struggle to win support in Congress.

euronews.title: Iconic London hotel Dukes is set to reopen in mid-2027
euronews.description: The property, which is home to the legendary martini spot Dukes Bar, will be operated by Minor Hotels.

euronews.title: Mobile ebola laboratory cuts diagnosis times for patients in Congo
euronews.description: A mobile laboratory in Butembo, eastern DRC, is cutting Ebola testing times, with results available within 24 hours and sometimes as quickly as six.

euronews.title: France and Germany lead push to keep military space powers in national hands
euronews.description: Germany and France are among seven countries calling for the proposed European Space Shield to be rebuilt around protecting EU space systems – with military space capabilities kept national.

rfi.title: Ethiopia's new rebel war redraws alliances across the Horn of Africa
rfi.description: Ethiopia and Eritrea have cut diplomatic ties as a new rebel offensive grips northern Ethiopia, putting two countries that fought together during the last Tigray war on opposing sides. Ethiopia accuses its neighbour of supporting a new anti-government alliance.

rfi.title: Farmers unite worldwide against what they call ‘chemical colonisation’
rfi.description: Farmers and activists around the world are mobilising on Saturday for an international day of action against pesticides – denouncing products sold by major agrochemical companies that they say are damaging their health and destroying their livelihoods.

rfi.title: Bardella under pressure as new evidence emerges in anti-Semitic messages row
rfi.description: Jordan Bardella, president of France's far-right National Rally party, is under growing pressure as new technical evidence challenges his denials over anti-Semitic messages allegedly sent during his teenage years.

rfi.title: France closes 400 schools as student unrest over conditions continues
rfi.description: France has closed hundreds of secondary schools amid violent student protests, as ministers urged parents to keep children away from blockades and warned families could be billed for damage.

rfi.title: Nations League: Italy reel in France to spoil Zidane's homecoming party
rfi.description: Italy ended Zinedine Zidane's triumphant start to life as France head coach on Friday night with a 1-1 draw at the Stade de France in the Nations League.

rfi.title: Moroccan intelligence accused of spying on journalists and human rights activists
rfi.description: Morocco’s domestic intelligence service has deployed Pegasus spyware and hidden cameras in a sweeping campaign of surveillance against journalists and human rights activists, according to a report by Amnesty International.

rfi.title: World powers gather in Pacific to chart climate battle
rfi.description: World powers are flying delegates to the Pacific to haggle over the fight against global warming, and to see the plight of island nations surrounded by a rising ocean.

rfi.title: More than half of Europe exposed to extreme heat stress this summer
rfi.description: A record 52 percent of the European continent was exposed to intense heat stress during the summer of 2026, according to the European Union’s Copernicus climate monitoring service. The season saw Europe experience four of its 10 worst heatwaves on record.

rfi.title: EU approves tougher migration rules in latest push to tighten borders
rfi.description: European Union interior ministers agreed on Thursday to toughen the bloc's migration policies, particularly on returns of undocumented migrants. They also want to step up social media monitoring to prevent further mass movements of people after the crisis in the Spanish exclave of Ceuta this summer.

rfi.title: From London to Les Bleus: Olise proves his potential in Zidane's new wave
rfi.description: On a cloudy night in Brussels, Michael Olise took nine seconds to highlight his genius and maintain the euphoria around France's new head coach Zinedine Zidane.

rfi.title: France launches €35m fund to attract private investment to overseas territories
rfi.description: France has launched a €35 million investment fund to attract private capital to businesses in its overseas territories, as the government seeks to shift the focus from subsidies towards growth, innovation and regional expansion.

rfi.title: Family feud yields sour grapes at French drinks empire Castel
rfi.description: A court in Singapore is preparing to rule on a power struggle at the Castel Group, a family-run French beverage business that has grown to be one of the largest drinks companies in Europe and Africa – and is currently the subject of a dispute between two of the founder's relatives and the CEO, the first person outside the Castel family to run the multibillion-euro business.

rfi.title: Nuremberg trials: 'When you see these people in the dock, the world changes'
rfi.description: The Nuremberg trials, held by the Allied powers after the Second World War to prosecute prominent Nazis for war crimes, came to an end on 1 October, 1946. The 10 months of hearings marked a turning point in international criminal justice, paving the way for the International Criminal Court. Bruno Cathala, who helped build the ICC, tells RFI how the Nuremberg trials changed the course of history.

rfi.title: Infantino loses Swiss backing for campaign to remain Fifa chief
rfi.description: Gianni Infantino's drive to remain boss at world football's governing body Fifa was under threat on Thursday after his own country's football association withdrew its support.

rfi.title: 'Catastrophic': Swiss glaciers lose fifth of mass in five years
rfi.description: Switzerland's glaciers, which are disproportionately impacted by climate change, have lost nearly 20 percent of their mass in five years, experts said Thursday, with 2026 registering the second-biggest melt on record.

rfi.title: Paris court jails six men for manslaughter over mass drowning in Channel
rfi.description: A Paris court has found six men guilty of ​manslaughter over the deaths of 27 people in the Channel in 2021 – the worst mass drowning on record involving migrants in the narrow waterway separating France and Britain.

rfi.title: Argentine leader Milei on mission to beef up economy during Paris visit
rfi.description: As part of a four-day visit aimed at promoting investment opportunities in Argentina, where the economy is flailing, the country's President Javier Milei will address the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development on Thursday and meet with French President Emmanuel Macron.

rfi.title: France and UK scrap migrant exchange deal after one-year trial
rfi.description: A year-old deal between France and Britain to return migrants crossing the Channel illegally on small boats has come to an end, the UK interior ministry said Wednesday.

lemonde.title: Blocage des lycées : le mouvement s’enracine, l’éducation nationale amorce le dialogue
lemonde.description: Malgré une légère décrue des actions vendredi 2 octobre, les lycéens restent fortement mobilisés. Le ministre Edouard Geffray a reçu syndicats, représentants lycéens et parents d’élèves et promis d’engager un « travail sur la démocratie scolaire ».

lemonde.title: Budget 2027 : ce que propose le gouvernement pour mettre à contribution les retraités
lemonde.description: Le gouvernement veut réaliser 5,5 milliards d’euros d’économies sur les pensionnés, mais se dit ouvert à la discussion avec les parlementaires pour définir les modalités du tour de vis.

lemonde.title: France-Italie : soirée frustrante pour les Bleus, malgré le retour triomphal de Zidane au Stade de France
lemonde.description: Les Tricolores ont concédé un match nul face à l’Italie (1-1) en Ligue des nations. Loin du scénario rêvé par les supporteurs, qui entendaient fêter le premier match à domicile du nouveau sélectionneur.

lemonde.title: Sous la pression de Donald Trump, le G7 annonce un déblocage de 100 millions de barils de pétrole
lemonde.description: La menace d’un embargo américain sur les exportations de gazole a précipité les discussions autour des pistes susceptibles de freiner l’envolée des prix.

lemonde.title: A Paris, pour son premier budget, le maire Emmanuel Grégoire accusé de « marchandiser » la ville
lemonde.description: Le maire socialiste de la capitale assume de se tourner davantage vers le privé pour continuer à maintenir un haut niveau d’investissement. « Paris n’est pas à vendre », met en garde l’opposition.

lemonde.title: Après le succès de la série « The Bear », l’acteur Jeremy Allen White s’impose au cinéma
lemonde.description: Son rôle de chef sensible et tourmenté dans la série « The Bear » a propulsé l’acteur new-yorkais de 35 ans dans une nouvelle dimension. Réalisateurs, stylistes, publicitaires… le cinéma comme la mode s’arrachent sa douceur virile. Après avoir endossé le rôle de Bruce Springsteen, Jeremy Allen White est le journaliste Jeff Horowitz dévoilant les dérives de Facebook dans « The Social Reckoning », d’Aaron Sorkin, en salle le 7 octobre.

lemonde.title: Guerre en Ukraine : le pari risqué de Donald Trump d’assouplir les sanctions contre la Russie
lemonde.description: Le président des Etats-Unis veut alléger les sanctions pesant sur Moscou contre la libération de prisonniers politiques. Ce marchandage, censé bâtir la paix, pourrait soulever l’hostilité de l’Ukraine et de ses alliés.

lemonde.title: Royaume-Uni : deux Iraniens inculpés pour un projet d’acte terroriste contre la communauté juive à Manchester
lemonde.description: Les suspects, deux hommes d’une trentaine d’années, sont notamment soupçonnés par la police britannique d’avoir « communiqué avec d’autres personnes via des applications chiffrées afin d’obtenir les composants nécessaires à l’assemblage d’un engin explosif artisanal ».

lemonde.title: Aux Etats-Unis, la croissance reste vive mais elle crée moins d’emplois
lemonde.description: Le pays n’a généré que 29 000 postes au mois de septembre, bien en dessous des 80 000 anticipés par les analystes. Le secteur du soin a porté l’essentiel de ces créations quand celui des services financiers continue de plonger en la matière.

lemonde.title: Christa Pike : la condamnée à mort se trouve sous respirateur après son exécution ratée
lemonde.description: Les médecins s’efforcent d’éliminer de l’organisme de la quinquagénaire les deux doses de pentobarbital, le produit létal qui lui a été injecté, selon ses avocats.

lemonde.title: Royaume-Uni : un homme de 28 ans inculpé pour un projet terroriste visant notamment Nigel Farage
lemonde.description: Joshua Kerry, Britannique de 28 ans qui doit comparaître mercredi à Londres, est accusé d’avoir préparé pendant plus de deux ans des actes de terrorisme, visant notamment le chef de Reform UK, Nigel Farage.

lemonde.title: Ebola en RDC : la pire épidémie de l’histoire du pays franchit la barre des 4 000 morts
lemonde.description: Le pays fait face à une flambée inédite du virus mais la présence de groupes armés et la défiance d’une partie des populations locales entravent la riposte. Le chef de la diplomatie française, Jean-Noël Barrot, est sur place pour marquer le soutien de Paris aux autorités locales et aux humanitaires.

lemonde.title: Au Sénat, tensions autour du groupe de Claude Malhuret

lemonde.title: Laurent Nuñez promet aux pompiers 1 milliard d’euros d’aide supplémentaire sur cinq ans pour renforcer leurs moyens
lemonde.description: Selon le ministre de l’intérieur, un « relèvement exceptionnel » de la taxe sur les conventions d’assurances, prévu dans le projet de loi de finances, permettra de dégager annuellement 200 millions d’euros sur cinq ans. « C’est une orientation politique intéressante », a jugé le syndicat de pompiers professionnels FA SPP-PATS.

lemonde.title: Au Texas, la justice suspend le chantier frontalier de l’administration Trump dans le parc national de Big Bend
lemonde.description: Une juge fédérale a suspendu jusqu’à nouvel ordre les travaux de construction de barrières, de routes de patrouille et d’équipements de surveillance dans ce parc situé à la frontière avec le Mexique. Un chantier à 1,7 milliard de dollars contesté par des organisations environnementales et des acteurs locaux.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : les services de renseignements ukrainiens s’attendent à une intensification des « opérations hybrides » russes en Europe
lemonde.description: Il pourrait s’agir d’« opérations hybrides visant à saper l’aide à l’Ukraine et à affaiblir les capacités de l’Alliance », qui pourrait notamment viser des stations Starlink. Par ailleurs, à Kiev, le pont Pivdenny « a de nouveau été touché », a annoncé le maire, vendredi soir. La circulation y avait été suspendue, en début de journée, après des bombardements russes.

france24fr.title: Tunisie : le décret-loi 54 assoupli, la peine de prison pour une première infraction disparaît
france24fr.description: En Tunisie, le décret 54, un texte promulgué par la Présidence de la République en 2022, a été amendé mercredi 30 septembre. Ce texte supposé lutté contre la diffusion de fausses informations et de rumeurs sur les réseaux sociaux a été surtout utilisé ces dernières années pour réprimer la liberté d'expression dans le pays

france24fr.title: Contestation lycéenne, récupération politique et budget : peut-on encore éviter le chaos?
france24fr.description: Cette semaine la contestation lycéenne a pris une ampleur nationale. Et cette colère arrive au pire moment pour le gouvernement puisqu’il vient de présenter son projet de budget pour 2027. Jusqu’où ira la crise ? On en parle avec Virginie Martin, politologue et professeure à Kedge Business School.

france24fr.title: "Costard en kevlar" : les rédactions de 39 médias condamnent les propos de M. Le Pen contre Mediapart
france24fr.description: Les sociétés de rédacteurs et de journalistes d'une quarantaine de médias français, dont France 24 et RFI, ont publié vendredi une tribune condamnant les récentes déclarations de la candidate à la présidentielle du Rassemblement national Marine Le Pen visant le site d'investigation Mediapart. Elles dénoncent de "violentes tentatives d'intimidation" contre la liberté de la presse, qu'elles jugent "particulièrement inquiétantes pour le droit à l'information auquel peut prétendre la population d'un

france24fr.title: 🔴 Ligue des nations : les Bleus tenus en échec par l'Italie pour la première de Zidane à domicile
Ligue des nations : les Bleus tenus en échec par l'Italie pour la première de Zidane à domicile
france24fr.description: L'équipe de France a été neutralisée par l'Italie (1-1), vendredi soir, en Ligue des nations au stade de France à Saint-Denis. Pour la première de Zinedine Zidane à domicile en tant que sélectionneur, les Bleus ont longtemps cru pouvoir l'emporter avant de céder face à la Squadra Azzurra et de se faire peur en terminant le match en infériorité numérique.

france24fr.title: Étudiante "blessée par des agresseurs", "personnel aspergé d'essence" : le gouvernement a menti ?
france24fr.description: Depuis le début de la semaine, le mouvement de blocage des lycées prend de l'ampleur et de nombreuses images de violence y sont associées. L'occasion pour les responsables politiques de se livrer une bataille sur ce sujet. Le Premier ministre Sébastien Lecornu a assuré qu'une étudiante avait été agressée. Le ministre de l'Éducation Nationale Edouard Geffray que des personnels avaient été aspergés d'essence. Est-ce vrai ? Décryptage dans Info Intox avec Jules BOITEAU.

france24fr.title: Clap de fin pour Cristiano Ronaldo ?
france24fr.description: Le Portugal a remporté, jeudi face au Danemark, son troisième match consécutif de Ligue des nations – les deux dernières rencontres ayant été gagnées sans la participation de Cristiano Ronaldo. Une sortie ratée de la part du quintuple Ballon d'or, qui a quitté le rassemblement mercredi soir.

france24fr.title: Brexit : "Trop gros, trop tôt" pour envisager un retour du Royaume-Uni au sein de l'UE
france24fr.description: Dix ans après le référendum sur le Brexit, l'hypothèse d'un rapprochement entre Londres et Bruxelles revient dans le débat politique britannique. Le Premier ministre Andy Burnham a même évoqué la possibilité d'une réintégration du Royaume-Uni au sein l'UE. Si la perspective d'un "Breturn" semble encore éloignée, "il y a certainement beaucoup mieux à faire que de maintenir le statu quo", estime Sébastien Maillard, conseiller spécial à l'Institut Jacques Delors.

france24fr.title: Vincent Duclert: "la dédiabolisation du RN a littéralement volé en éclats"
france24fr.description: La question de l'antisémitisme a percuté la campagne à la présidentielle, avec les révélations de Mediapart au sujet des écrits passés de Jordan Bardella. La dédiabolisation de l'extrême droite française n'était-elle qu'un leurre? Pourquoi cette persistance de l'antisémitisme au sein d'une partie de la classe politique et de la société française ? L'historien Vincent Duclert, auteur de "La philosophie contre l'antisémitisme" (éditions PUF), était l'Invité d'Au Cœur de l'Info.

france24fr.title: Mobilisation lycéenne : face aux débordements, le maintien de l'ordre en question
france24fr.description: Depuis qu'il s'est élargi, le mouvement de protestation des lycéens est rythmé par de nombreux débordements. En réaction, la présence policière apparaît comme massive, et plusieurs manifestants dénoncent des faits de violences. Un climat tendu, attisé par l'assimilation du mouvement à des "violences urbaines", selon le spécialiste Olivier Cahn.

france24fr.title: Non, la police nationale n’a pas lâché un chien sur des lycéens à Lille
france24fr.description: Sur la base d’une vidéo circulant sur les réseaux sociaux, la police nationale a été accusée d’avoir lâché un chien sur les élèves qui avaient organisé mardi le blocus du lycée César Baggio, à Lille. Or, selon les journalistes qui couvraient l'événement, le chien visible dans la vidéo n'appartenait pas aux forces de l’ordre.

france24fr.title: Ghana : Carlos Queiroz démissionne après cinq mois sur le banc des Black Stars
france24fr.description: Carlos Queiroz a annoncé jeudi quitter son de sélectionneur du Ghana. Après seulement cinq mois sur le banc des Black Stars, l'entraîneur portugais paie notamment les résultats décevants de sa sélection.

france24fr.title: Jugé coupable de "graves" infractions financières, Manchester City fait appel
france24fr.description: Après avoir été jugé coupable de "graves" infractions financières, le club de Manchester City a annoncé vendredi avoir fait appel dans cette affaire aux "conséquences majeures pour l'intégrité" du jeu, selon la Fédération anglaise de football.

france24fr.title: Chine et États-Unis : rivaux ou partenaires ?
france24fr.description: Rencontre au sommet. Le 23 septembre dernier, le président américain Donald Trump recevait son homologue chinois Xi Jinping en grande pompe à Washington. Il s'agissait de sa première visite à la Maison Blanche depuis dix ans, mais de sa troisième rencontre avec le président américain en un an. Derrière l'apparat, peu de résultats. Nos invités reviennent sur cette rencontre entre superpuissances.

france24fr.title: Détroit d'Ormuz : pourquoi le grand retour du pétrole ne suffit pas à faire baisser les prix
france24fr.description: En septembre, les exportations de pétrole depuis la région du Golfe ont atteint des niveaux quasi similaires à ceux d’avant le début de la guerre américano-israélienne contre l’Iran. Le président américain Donald Trump avait promis une baisse des prix dès que la menace iranienne sur le détroit d’Ormuz ne ferait plus autant d’effet sur les flux de pétrole. Ce n’est pourtant pas ce qui se passe.

france24fr.title: Intelligence artificielle : un affolement "calculé" ?
france24fr.description: L'intelligence artificielle menace-t-elle l'espèce humaine à l'échelle d'une décennie ? La prophétie d'un employé démissionnaire d'Anthropic a déclenché un vent de panique chez les géants de la tech américaine. Angoisse sincère ou simple calcul économique ? Pour en parler, notre invité : Michel Lévy-Provençal, entrepreneur dans le numérique et fondateur de Qapten.com.

france24fr.title: Brésil : Lula, un président candidat à 80 ans
france24fr.description: À bientôt 81 ans, Lula veut montrer qu'il a l'énergie pour présider encore le Brésil. Après de la prison, une condamnation pour corruption, un cancer de la peau, il brigue un quatrième mandat à la tête du pays. Les 4 et 25 octobre, il affrontera Flavio Bolsonaro dans un duel qui s'annonce serré.

france24fr.title: Maciej Witucki : "Taxer les superprofits, certains États comme la Pologne le font déjà"
france24fr.description: Cette semaine, Caroline De Camaret reçoit Maciej Witucki, président de BusinessEurope depuis le 1er juillet 2026. Plus grande organisation patronale d'Europe, BusinessEurope représente plus de 40 fédérations patronales nationales issues de 35 pays. Polonais de nationalité, il dresse avec nous un bilan du paysage entrepreneurial européen, de ses défis et de ses pistes d'amélioration.

zeit.title: Zentrale Feier in Bremen: Wegner: Jahrestag der Deutschen Einheit Anlass zur Freude
Ähnlich simpel wie «hallo123»: Schalke weit vorn - im Negativranking schlechter Passwörter
Zum 3. Oktober: Osten, Westen, Einheit? Fünf Fakten zum Stand der Dinge
Wird die Million geknackt?: Rund 950.000 Besucher: Landesgartenschau in Ellwangen endet
Saarland: Gewerkschaft der Polizei fordert mehr Personal und Technik
Justiz: Asylverfahren in Hessen dauern deutlich kürzer
Branchenzahlen: Den Verlagen kommen die Leser abhanden
Tag der offenen Moschee: Viele NRW-Moscheen laden zum Besuch ein
Elisabeth Kaiser: Ostbeauftragte schlägt ostdeutsche Frau als Staatsoberhaupt vor
zeit.description: Warum sollte die nächste Bundespräsidentin nicht »eine kluge Frau aus Ostdeutschland« sein, fragt die Ostbeauftragte der Bundesregierung. Sie hält die Zeit für reif.

zeit.title: Wiedervereinigung: Kluft zwischen Einkommen in Ost- und Westdeutschland nimmt weiter zu
zeit.description: Im Osten haben Haushalte rund 7.000 Euro weniger netto zur Verfügung als im Westen des Landes. Laut einer Studie stockt auch die Angleichung der ostdeutschen Wirtschaft.

zeit.title: USA: Zum Tode verurteilte Frau nach gescheiterter Hinrichtung bewusstlos
zeit.description: Die 50-jährige Christa Pike befindet sich nach dem gescheiterten Hinrichtungsversuch in Tennessee weiter in kritischem Zustand. Sie hat zuvor zwei Giftspritzen überlebt.

zeit.title: Energiekrise: USA haben Diesel-Exportstopp laut Donald Trump nie ernsthaft geplant
zeit.description: Nach dem G7-Beschluss zur Freigabe strategischer Ölreserven hat der US-Präsident Drohungen gegen die EU widerrufen. Er habe nie vorgehabt, Dieselexporte zu stoppen.

zeit.title: US-Küstenwache: Schiff mit Treibstoff für Kuba von US-Küstenwache gestoppt
zeit.description: Die US-Küstenwache hat im September ein Schiff mit einer Treibstofflieferung für Kuba abgefangen. Auf der Insel verschärft sich die Energiekrise.

zeit.title: Schulproteste in Frankreich: Schülervertreter in Frankreich distanzieren sich von Gewalt
zeit.description: Nach einem Treffen mit dem Bildungsminister distanzieren sich Vertreter der Schulproteste von Gewalt. Schüler und Gewerkschaften wollen die Proteste weiterführen.

zeit.title: G7-Staaten: Reiche sieht Energiereserve auch nach G7-Freigabe ausreichend gedeckt
zeit.description: Um die Energiepreise zu senken, haben die G7 beschlossen, strategische Reserven freizugeben. Für die Energieversorgung bestehe kein Risiko, versichert Katherina Reiche.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Iran-Krieg: Rohöltanker vor der Küste Omans angegriffen
nzz.description: Die USA und Iran befinden sich seit Februar 2026 im Kriegszustand. Zwar haben die beiden Länder eine Waffenruhe vereinbart, doch Donald Trump hat diese Anfang Juli für beendet erklärt. Die neuesten Entwicklungen im Ticker.

nzz.title: Sie atmete nach zwei Dosen weiter: Verurteilte Mörderin überlebt Hinrichtungsversuch in den USA
nzz.description: Christa Pike sollte am Mittwoch hingerichtet werden. Doch die Vollstreckung scheiterte, sie befindet sich in kritischen Zustand im Spital. Der Gliedstaat Tennessee steht nach dem zweiten gescheiterten Hinrichtungsversuch innerhalb weniger Monate in der Kritik.

nzz.title: Olise-Traumtor zu wenig: Italien erkämpft sich in Paris ein Remis in der Nations League
nzz.description: Das erste Heimspiel von Zinédine Zidane als Nationaltrainer Frankreichs bleibt trotz einem Traumtor von Bayern-Star Michael Olise ohne Sieger. Bosnien-Herzegowina verabschiedet Edin Dzeko.

nzz.title: Der mutmassliche Mörder der britischen Politikerin Ann Widdecombe hatte offenbar weitere Anschläge geplant
nzz.description: Laut der britischen Polizei nahm der Beschuldigte in seinen Terrorplänen unter anderem den Reform-Chef Nigel Farage ins Visier. Nun wurde er angeklagt.

nzz.title: Fast 2000 Festnahmen an einem Tag: Die Schülerproteste in Frankreich weiten sich zum Flächenbrand aus
nzz.description: Die Unruhen wegen Lehrermangel und maroder Schulen in Frankreich eskalieren. Vielfach ist unklar, ob es überhaupt noch Schüler sind, die Feuer legen. Zum Gesicht der Bewegung ist Ryad Rani geworden – ein 18-jähriger Aktivist mit Verbindung zu La France insoumise.

nzz.title: MELDUNGEN ZÜRICH - Astrophysiker Zurbuchen wechselt von der ETH zur Raumfahrtfirma Blue Origin
nzz.description: Die neuesten Meldungen aus dem Kanton.

nzz.title: Hohe Treibstoffpreise: Die Staaten der G-7 wollen Dieselreserven freigeben
nzz.description: Seit Tagen droht Trump den Europäern. Er werde sie vom amerikanischen Diesel abhängen, wenn sie nichts gegen die hohen Preise unternähmen. Nun reagieren die grossen Industriestaaten.

nzz.title: Das biometrische Klassenzimmer: Usbekistan will seine Schüler mit KI überwachen
nzz.description: Die Hauptstadt Taschkent stattet 26 Schulen mit Smart-Kameras aus. Offiziell will der Staat die Bildung stärken. Die pädagogische Sorge weicht in diesem Experiment aber autoritärer Kontrolle.

nzz.title: Bruchlandung in der Wohnungspolitik: Nach einer Niederlage des Regierungschefs Sánchez steht Spanien wohl vor Neuwahlen
nzz.description: Die Regierung verliert im Parlament die Abstimmung um ihr Massnahmenpaket zur Bekämpfung der Wohnungsnot. Die Protestbewegung will ihr Zeltlager abbrechen, aber die Demonstrationen ausweiten.

nzz.title: Bescheiden, diplomatisch, bodenständig: Guy Parmelin bleibt sich in seinem Abgang treu
nzz.description: Nach elf Jahren im Bundesrat will Guy Parmelin Platz machen für unverbrauchte Kräfte. Der Wirtschaftsminister tritt mit versöhnlichen Tönen ab, aber auch mit einer deutlichen Warnung.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Wohnungskrise in Spanien: Die sozialistische Regierung scheitert kläglich
nzz.description: Zwei Dekrete sollten im Eilverfahren Spaniens Wohnungsnot entschärfen. Doch Pedro Sánchez bekommt für seine unausgereiften Ideen keine Mehrheit. Zu Recht. Seine Regierung ist an ihrem Ende angelangt.

nzz.title: MELDUNGEN POLIZEI - Schmuggler versteckt Kokain in Lollipops und fliegt am Flughafen auf +++ Die Stadtpolizei Zürich verlässt das Netzwerk X und ist neu auf Whatsapp
nzz.description: Die neuesten Polizeimeldungen aus der Schweiz.

nzz.title: MELDUNGEN WIRTSCHAFT - Zurich schliesst Kauf des Spezialversicherers Beazley ab +++ Rohstoffhändler Gunvor ändert seinen Namen und verlegt Hauptsitz
Europäische Union kritisiert obligatorischen Strafregisterauszug für EU-Bürger
nzz.description: Die EU erwarte, dass sich auch die Schweiz an ihre Verpflichtungen halte, sagt ihr Botschafter Andreas Künne. Vom Ständerat beschlossene Verschärfungen bei der Personenfreizügigkeit seien nicht hilfreich.

nzz.title: Ein Tankrabatt gegen teuren Diesel? Deshalb sind ausgerechnet die Schweizer Linksparteien strikt dagegen
nzz.description: Trotz hoher Treibstoffpreise wollen Schweizer Parteien keine staatlichen Eingriffe – mit einer Ausnahme: Die SVP fordert breite Entlastungen für Autofahrer.

nzz.title: Angriffe auf Brücken, Schulen, Rechenzentren: Russland will Kiew unbewohnbar machen
nzz.description: Russland zerstört seit viereinhalb Jahren gezielt die zivile Infrastruktur der Ukraine. Die gegenwärtige Kampagne erreicht jedoch ein neues Ausmass. Besonders in Kiew wird die Lage schwierig.

observador.title: 2h. Defesa da Polónia redige lei de preparação para guerra
observador.description: Esta lei pode incluir o destacamento de tropas para pontos considerados “sensíveis” dentro da NATO. Ainda, doações de oligarcas russos correspondem a mais de 1% do Orçamento do Estado da Rússia.

observador.title: 1h.  Flydubai. Suspeito tinha sido já afastado por companhia
observador.description: O suspeito do ataque à Flydubai já tinha sido afastado pela companhia aérea nacional de Omã. Ainda, Donald Trump não vai proibir as exportações de combustível para a Europa

observador.title: Manchester. Dois acusados de planear atentado contra judeus
observador.description: Dois homens têm origem iraniana, sendo um deles refugiado. Ministro veio relacionar ataque com imigração ilegal. Tinham construído bomba e pesquisado alvos.

observador.title: O caso das gémeas mostra a importância de um telefone no SNS
observador.description: Quem tiver nascido nas famílias certas, quem tiver estudado nas escolas certas, quem tiver os amigos certos e quem tiver entrado no partido certo, terá na agenda o número certo de telemóvel e salva-se

observador.title: O Ocidente que resistiu a bordo de um Boeing
observador.description: Os israelitas a bordo, com a indispensável ajuda do comandante, perceberam que ou tratavam do assunto ou o assunto trataria deles. Já haverá "activistas" a exigir a sua punição.

observador.title: O Cónego Jeremias e a laicidade do Estado
observador.description: A Constituição nunca diz que Portugal é um país laico, apenas que é não confessional. E não confessional não quer dizer laicista

observador.title: Igual ao mesmo
observador.description: Será que as coisas que vemos com os olhos abertos continuam a existir da mesma maneira quando os fechamos?

observador.title: Microsoft alerta: Portugal no top 20 de ciberataques
observador.description: No 1.º semestre de 2026, Portugal ficou no 55.º lugar mundial em impacto de atividade cibernética maliciosa. A IA acelera as ameaças — e também a defesa.

observador.title: BE questiona Governo sobre medidas de proteção do rio Leça
observador.description: Fabian Figueiredo quer saber que medidas estão a ser tomadas para identificar focos de poluição, incluindo as ETAR de Ermesinde, Parada e Moreira.

observador.title: O que é que estes miúdos andam a fazer?
observador.description: Há centenas de crianças em Lisboa privadas da escola, a nossa primeira obrigação enquanto adultos é perceber o que se pode fazer para que regressem.

observador.title: Izana e a Cabana dos muitos Fios
observador.description: Izana levou três anos a erguer a Cabana de Ler do Shogun. Não deixou, contudo, de contar histórias.

observador.title: Maçonaria: os Devoristas
observador.description: Parece-me que seria útil e saudável, esclarecedor e fautor de transparência, se os detentores de cargos públicos, nomeadamente políticos, viessem à luz do dia afirmar-se como pedreiros-livres

observador.title: Guarda celebra legado do jesuíta Francisco de Pina
observador.description: De 6 a 8 de outubro, investigadores de Portugal e Vietname debatem o legado de Francisco de Pina, o guardense que no séc. XVII latinizou o vietnamita.

observador.title: É legal. E depois?
observador.description: Subvenção vitalícia: é difícil encontrar exemplo mais claro do problema de legislar em causa própria. A decisão terá todos os procedimentos legais, mas o conflito de interesses não desaparece.

observador.title: Quem ganha com o enfraquecimento da escola europeia?
observador.description: A escola dificilmente colapsará de um dia para o outro. O risco é outro: o desgaste lento e silencioso de uma das instituições mais importantes da democracia.

observador.title: Esquecemos a COVID. Mas o inverno não se esqueceu de nós!
observador.description: Cinco anos depois da pandemia, abandonámos quase todas as medidas que aprendemos. Algumas mereciam ter sobrevivido ao vírus — não por medo, mas por saúde pública.

observador.title: O futebol, o Ronaldo e a metáfora explicativa
observador.description: Eis então, uma pequena metáfora... que nos ajuda a compreender que o futebol não é uma mera modalidade desportiva; o futebol é um facto social total!

observador.title: Testemunho de uma mãe alienada (III)
observador.description: Nesta história, continuaremos a acompanhar a forma como o filho mais velho se foi progressivamente afastando da mãe, enquanto a irmã permaneceu ligada a ela.

spiegel.title: Grok: Musks xAI setzt US-Gesetz gegen KI-Nacktbilder vorerst außer Kraft
spiegel.description: Sieg für Musk, Niederlage für den Opferschutz: xAI hat ein US-Verbotsgesetz gegen KI-generierte Nacktbilder vorerst gestoppt. Mehrere Länder gehen derweil eigene Wege gegen Grok.

spiegel.title: Sächsisches Innenministerium: Behörde löscht umstrittenen Post zu Berliner Linken
spiegel.description: Sachsens Innenministerium löscht einen umstrittenen Social-Media-Post über den Wahlsieg der Linkspartei in Berlin. In einer Stellungnahme erklärt Minister Schuster die Intention des Postings.

spiegel.title: Großbritannien: Verdächtiger im Mordfall Ann Widdecombe soll auch Anschlag auf Nigel Farage geplant haben
spiegel.description: Ihm wird bereits die Ermordung der ultrakonservativen Politikerin Ann Widdecombe vorgeworfen. Nun ergänzt die Staatsanwaltschaft die Vorwürfe gegen den 28 Jahre alten Briten.

spiegel.title: Christa Pike – Tennessee: Nach gescheiterter Hinrichtung intubiert und beatmet
spiegel.description: Sie überlebte die Hinrichtung durch zwei Giftspritzen, nun kämpft man im Krankenhaus um Christa Pikes Leben. Ihre Anwälte erheben schwere Vorwürfe.

spiegel.title: Iran-Krieg: Warum gelangt wieder so viel Öl durch die Straße von Hormus?
spiegel.description: Immer mehr Tanker passieren das Nadelöhr, obwohl Iran Dutzende Drohnen und Raketen pro Woche in der Meerenge verschießt. Das sind die Hintergründe.

spiegel.title: Coldmirror: YouTuberin empfindet »keine Liebe mehr« für Harry Potter
spiegel.description: Die YouTuberin Coldmirror wurde ab 2006 berühmt mit Neusynchronisationen. Darunter der Millenial-Hit »Harry Potter und ein Stein«. Nun erzählt sie, wie sie sich von Harry distanziert hat.

spiegel.title: Saudi-Arabien: Turki bin Faisal drängt auf deutsche Rolle in Militärbündnis
spiegel.description: Saudi-Arabien schmiedet eine Militärallianz gegen die Huthis im Jemen – zusammen mit Briten und Franzosen. Nun fordert Ex-Geheimdienstchef Turki bin Faisal al Saud auch eine deutsche Beteiligung.

spiegel.title: Jemen: Welternährungsprogramm befürchtet verheerende Hungersnot
spiegel.description: Die Kämpfe zwischen der Huthi-Miliz und Saudi-Arabien eskalieren. Das Welternährungsprogramm warnt, dass darunter vor allem die Menschen im Jemen leiden könnten.

spiegel.title: Rente: Rechnungshof warnt vor wachsender Belastung des Bundeshaushalts
spiegel.description: Durch die geplanten Reformen könnten fast 46 Prozent der Steuereinnahmen für die Rente verbraucht werden. Der Haushalt könne zu einseitig beansprucht werden, mahnen die Rechnungsprüfer.

spiegel.title: Türkei: Kleinanleger bangen um ihr Geld – während Erdoğan-Vertraute Millionen gemacht haben soll
spiegel.description: Ein Börsenskandal erschüttert die Türkei: Hunderttausende könnten ihr Erspartes verlieren, Erdoğans Stellvertreterin in der AKP-Führung soll hohe Gewinne gemacht haben. Gab es Rückendeckung aus der Politik?

spiegel.title: Frankreich: Unruhen an 560 Schulen – Gymnasiasten distanzieren sich von Gewalt
spiegel.description: In Frankreich protestieren Schülerinnen und Schüler für bessere Bildung, doch die Demonstrationen eskalieren. In Paris brennen zwei Schuleingänge. Der Bildungsminister sucht den Dialog, doch die Proteste gehen weiter.

spiegel.title: Katherina Reiche drängt Gaskonzerne zum Einspeichern
spiegel.description: Die Bundeswirtschaftsministerin hat nach SPIEGEL-Informationen sechs Konzernvertreter aufgefordert, mehr Gas einzuspeichern. Offenbar mit mäßigem Erfolg.

spiegel.title: BKA: Junge »Killer-Kinder« als billige Täter für »Violence as a Service« - SPIEGEL TV
spiegel.description: Die Organisierte Kriminalität setzt immer häufiger junge »Wegwerf-Täter« ein. Für ein paar Tausend Euro werden sie auf Gegner angesetzt, schießen oder werfen Brandsätze. Das BKA nennt das Phänomen »Violence as a Service«.

spiegel.title: EU-Parlament und das Verbrenner-Aus: Autoindustrie sucht Nähe zur extremen Rechten
spiegel.description: Das EU-Parlament entscheidet bald, wie stark das Aus vom Verbrenner aufgeweicht wird. Es könnte auf Stimmen der Rechten ankommen. In Brüssel haben Vertreter der Autolobby kaum noch Berührungsängste.

spiegel.title: FASD: Alkohol in der Schwangerschaft erzeugt Kosten in Milliardenhöhe
spiegel.description: Wenn Schwangere Alkohol trinken, kann das schwere Folgen für das Kind haben. Einer Studie zufolge entstehen aber auch enorme gesellschaftliche Kosten. Eine Expertin mahnt, daraus die richtigen Schlüsse zu ziehen.

spiegel.title: Sarah Kuttner sagt nach Krebsvorsorgetermin Lesung ab
spiegel.description: Sarah Kuttner hat nach einem Arztbesuch einen Auftritt in Göttingen abgesagt. Man müsse nun herausfinden, »wie groß die Kacke tatsächlich ist«, sagt sie auf Instagram. »Aufmunternde Worte« kann sie gerade nicht gebrauchen.

spiegel.title: Doro Pesch verbrachte in den Achtzigern die Nächte mit Obdachlosen

phys-org.title: Why tenants choose to move out in connection with renovation
phys-org.description: One in three tenants who moved out of a municipal rental apartment in Gothenburg in connection with renovation said the renovation was a main reason for their decision, and many of them moved out even before construction began. A new study from Chalmers University of Technology shows that concerns about disruption, uncertainty and unclear information can be just as important as rent increases.

phys-org.title: Team selected for NASA program to explore potential lunar cave
phys-org.description: NASA has selected a Planetary Science Institute–led proposal to investigate whether a potentially large underground cave extends beyond the opening of a lunar pit. Such a cave may one day provide a safe haven for astronauts to escape the radiation and extreme temperature swings present at the lunar surface.

phys-org.title: Changes to platinum surface chemistry boost solar hydrogen production in organic photocatalysts
phys-org.description: Researchers from the LIMNO laboratory at EPFL have uncovered how different halides modify the surface chemistry of organic semiconductor nanoparticle photocatalysts. By controlling these phenomena, they have significantly improved the solar hydrogen production efficiency of these materials.

phys-org.title: Researchers turn America's scattered local laws into a free searchable database covering all 50 states
phys-org.description: America is a nation of local laws—millions of them. From noise ordinances and construction codes to rules about fishing licenses and roadside mango peddling, every town, city and county has its own set of regulations and unique way of doing things.

phys-org.title: Marine biologists discover new plankton off Oregon coast
phys-org.description: Nearly every morning when she was a doctoral student in the College of Arts and Sciences (CAS), Nicole Nakata, Ph.D. '23 (biology), would cross the street from the Oregon Institute of Marine Biology (OIMB) in Charleston, Ore., to the high-tide line of the Pacific Ocean. Her job was to catch microscopic brittle star plankton larvae from the incoming tidal current and bring them back to OIMB's labs to analyze under a microscope.

phys-org.title: Mowing less, spraying smarter give pollinators a boost
phys-org.description: Roadsides may not look like wildlife habitat, but a few simple changes to how they are maintained could turn them into much better places for pollinators. A new uOttawa-led study found that reducing mowing and herbicide use along rural roadsides led to a 45% jump in pollinator numbers and a 23% increase in the number of species found there.

phys-org.title: Scientists discover first type I superconductor that breaks time-reversal symmetry
phys-org.description: Superconductors are materials that conduct electricity with no resistance and expel magnetic fields when cooled to ultralow temperatures. And depending on their quantum structure, they can also showcase strange properties like magnetic levitation. But now things are getting a little weirder.

phys-org.title: On complex political issues, most Americans take shortcuts to simplicity
phys-org.description: A core assumption in any democracy is that citizens with access to information will make reasoned decisions on political candidates and policy issues. But a new study by UC Berkeley social scientists finds that Americans usually don't consider the full scope of difficult issues, instead basing their opinions on mental shortcuts that sidestep complexity.

phys-org.title: American beech trees may carry genetic resistance to deadly leaf disease
phys-org.description: A study led by scientists at the Holden Arboretum has found evidence that beech leaf disease (BLD) symptom development is genetically controlled, providing the first evidence that some American beech trees may have genetic resistance. This finding supports further investigation and development of breeding populations for BLD resistance. phys-org.title: Plasma-activated water tests show concentration matters for effective bacterial disinfection
phys-org.description: In a study published in npj Clean Water, researchers from EPFL investigated how Escherichia coli responds to different concentrations of plasma-activated water (PAW) under nutrient-rich conditions. The team combined conventional colony-forming unit (CFU) counting with nanomotion sensing, a technique that detects nanoscale oscillations produced by metabolically active bacteria.

phys-org.title: Ultrafast X-rays reveal how the light-responsive molecular switch azobenzene changes shape
phys-org.description: Azobenzene is one of the best-known molecules that can be switched between two forms by light. However, the question of how the molecule moves in the first few picoseconds (trillionths of a second) after it absorbs light has remained unresolved for nearly 50 years.

phys-org.title: Why a food poisoning bacterium can cause severe wound infections
phys-org.description: The toxin NheABC, produced by Bacillus cereus, is particularly active in the pH conditions found in open wounds. Researchers at Umeå University found that the toxin damages both cell membranes and mitochondria and helps the bacterium establish infection in wounded tissue.

phys-org.title: Motivation matters more than working memory for improving student math skills, study finds
phys-org.description: Why do some students become ever better at mathematics, while others plateau? Many people may think that mathematics is primarily about cognitive skills. A new study from the Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU) provides a more nuanced view. The paper is published in the journal Contemporary Educational Psychology.

phys-org.title: Computer-designed protein targets immune receptor linked to inflammation at new 'undruggable' site
phys-org.description: To sense their environment and respond accordingly, cells enlist membrane proteins as communication hubs, receiving molecular messages from outside and triggering responses inside. One of these proteins is Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4), an immune receptor that plays an essential role in protecting against infections. phys-org.title: Small changes can have a big impact on sustainability transitions
phys-org.description: In her dissertation, Hanna Entsalo examines how public policies, such as policy strategies and legislation, influence transitions toward the circular economy and sustainability. Entsalo works as a researcher in the Circular Economy Solutions Unit at the Finnish Environment Institute. Her work focuses on circular economy policy instruments, sustainability transitions and innovation policy, particularly at the national and EU levels.

phys-org.title: Black holes may grow quietly alongside galaxies even without violent mergers
phys-org.description: Astronomers analyzed 2,435 galaxies hosting actively feeding black holes using data from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI). Among them, they identified 546 "bulgeless" galaxies—systems with little or no central stellar bulge. Their paper, published in Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society, suggests that galaxies without a central bulge grow black holes just as effectively as galaxies that have one—a surprising sign that black holes don't need galaxy mergers to grow

phys-org.title: Scientists zero in on tiny particles to improve weather and air quality forecasts
phys-org.description: Aerosols are small particles suspended in our atmosphere. They come in many flavors: Wildfire smoke, pollen, desert dust, sea salt lofted by powerful storms, volcanic sulfates and emissions from engines and industrial processes are all examples.

phys-org.title: How does interdisciplinary collaboration work in practice? Three takeaways for teachers
phys-org.description: When we speak with Luyao Huang, her Ph.D. project at Leiden University is in full swing. Two papers—a systematic literature review and a case study on an interdisciplinary course—are already behind her. Next year, she will carry out a study in which teachers react to various scenarios. Today, Huang tells us about her most recent study: a deep dive into student collaboration.

undark.title: Podcast: Is ADHD Actually a Disorder?
undark.description: On Entanglements this week: Barbara Franke, a professor of molecular psychiatry at Radboud University in the Netherlands, and Edmund Sonuga-Barke, a developmental psychologist and a professor at King’s College London discuss whether ADHD should be considered a disorder.

undark.title: Podcast: Should We Put AI-Enabled Tech in Our Brains?
undark.description: Welcome to Season 3 of Entanglements! In our first episode, we discuss neural implants and AI with Judy Illes, a professor of neurology and neuroethics at the University of British Columbia, and Joseph J. Fins, a physician scientist and medical ethicist at Weill Cornell Medicine in New York.

undark.title: Engineering Animals to Grow Human Organs — But Not Human Minds
undark.description: Chimeras, or animals with human cells and tissues, are not new, and researchers have long used them to gain insights into diseases and even as a potential source of transplantable organs. But the research brings up thorny ethical questions regarding animal rights and the moral status of chimeric creatures.

undark.title: AI-Driven Biology Is Only as Good as the Data Beneath It
undark.description: Opinion | The biotech and pharma industries are pouring billions of dollars into AI-driven drug discovery and development. But the genomic data used to train AI models are often incomplete, contain errors, or lack contextual information — a quality issue that threatens to slow the pace of biological research.

undark.title: In Italy, What Earth Can Tell Us About Extraterrestrial Life
undark.description: Photo Essay | From sampling hydrothermal vents and abandoned mines to lab experiments that replicate Mars’ atmosphere, scientists are using what we know about life on Earth to understand how it may exist on other worlds. Italy, it seems, provides particularly fertile ground for such explorations.

undark.title: The Evolving Quest to Build Life in a Lab
undark.description: Scientists are trying to create new life, whether to understand how biology first developed on Earth, or design new cells from scratch.  But life hasn’t happened — at least not yet. And questions around safety, as well as what even constitutes life in the first place, continue to swirl.

undark.title: The Embryos That Don’t Come From Eggs and Sperm
undark.description: Human embryo models mimic the earliest development stages; they could offer a glimpse of the first weeks of pregnancy — a mysterious period for which natural embryos are seldom available — and potentially shed light on miscarriage, congenital anomalies, and other health issues. But how far should they go?

undark.title: Book Review: A Contrarian View of How Consciousness Evolved
undark.description: In “Natural Intelligence & the Logic of Consciousness,” neuroscientist Antonio Damasio argues against the conventional theory that consciousness stems from high-level brain function and cognition, which in turn leads to feelings. Instead, he writes, our basest feelings led us to our loftiest thoughts.

undark.title: AI Presents Science with a ‘Ship of Theseus’ Problem
undark.description: Opinion | AI is being integrated into every part of the scientific process, including education, publishing, and the research itself. What does it mean if every component of the enterprise gets replaced by AI tools over time? C. Brandon Ogbunu explores what happens when science gets stripped of human involvement.

undark.title: Interview: What Does the ‘I’ in AI Really Mean?
undark.description: Is it possible that AI is — or might one day become — truly intelligent? Undark posed the question to five experts in linguistics, computer science, cognitive science, and psychology. They offered very different answers, though they agreed that the term “intelligence” is vague and poorly suited to the debate.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s Great Oil Heist
proj-syn.description: Venezuela’s hopes for a democratic transition are fading as the US works to take control of its vast oil wealth. Billions in US and foreign investment could strengthen the chavista regime and give future American presidents powerful incentives to preserve the political status quo.

proj-syn.title: Global AI Oversight Now
proj-syn.description: AI is already concentrating enormous economic power and deepening existing inequalities, yet governments lack the institutions and expertise needed to govern it. They should establish an international AI body that can set standards and coordinate a collective response to threats no country can handle alone.

proj-syn.title: Climate Resilience Starts With Care
proj-syn.description: Climate shocks can disrupt services that millions of vulnerable people rely on, yet care is largely absent from adaptation plans and national funding estimates. Investing in climate-resilient care can prevent cascading health and economic crises while creating jobs and easing pressure on public budgets.

proj-syn.title: Conserving a Connected Ocean
proj-syn.description: For Seychelles and other countries across the Western Indian Ocean region, marine conservation is a fundamental component of national development. But the ocean observes no national borders, which makes international cooperation and common financing instruments essential.

proj-syn.title: Why Is the Global Economy So Resilient?
proj-syn.description: With the global economy having weathered major trade and energy shocks over the past two years, growth should improve in 2027, and inflation should fall. Although various political and policy-driven risks could change the outlook, they remain less likely than the relatively benign baseline scenario.

proj-syn.title: Closing Europe’s Dynamism Deficit
proj-syn.description: Europe has built an economic framework that protects yesterday’s champions at the expense of tomorrow’s potential winners. To remain competitive, sovereign, and secure in the 21st century, it will need a new model geared toward promoting domestic innovation and commercialization at scale.

proj-syn.title: America’s Looming Debt Reckoning
proj-syn.description: High debt levels become dangerous when rising interest rates push up borrowing costs and governments fail to respond. With little political appetite to rein in its federal deficit and ballooning debt, the United States risks finding itself with few options when the next war, recession, or financial crisis arrives.

proj-syn.title: The OECD Should Be Reclaimed, Not Abandoned
proj-syn.description: In recent years, the OECD has strayed from its core mission of coordinating economic policy among the US and its allies, instead building programs around gender budgeting and environmental justice. The Trump administration should use its leverage at the organization to return its focus to economics and national security.

proj-syn.title: Putin Is Testing NATO at Ukraine’s Borders
proj-syn.description: The Kremlin is determined to isolate Ukraine, which means not only breaking the will of the country’s backers, but also cutting it off physically by striking merchant ships, ports, and border crossings. These assaults cannot go unanswered, because they embolden Russian President Vladimir Putin to continue testing the West.

proj-syn.title: The Hard Road to a Middle-Power Order
proj-syn.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has challenged the world’s middle powers to build a better international order. Yet they are increasingly turning to coalitions of the willing and a patchwork of separate initiatives that risk entrenching zero-sum mindsets and making collective action harder.

proj-syn.title: The Sovereign Wealth Fund America Needs
proj-syn.description: Two recent proposals to establish a new US sovereign wealth fund would fail to make good on a good idea, because neither plan would produce a fund nearly large enough to meet America’s mounting financing needs. But a different approach, funded by Treasury sales, could.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s Vanity Summit With Xi
proj-syn.description: While expectations for the summit between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping were low, it was disappointing to watch them prioritize pageantry over substance. Trump’s cringe-worthy declarations of heartfelt admiration for Xi reflect his twisted sense that the trappings of power are power itself.

proj-syn.title: Human Rights and Populist Wrongs
proj-syn.description: For the first time, all the UK’s political parties on the right favor withdrawing from the European Convention on Human Rights. But the story of the Hillsborough Law shows how human-rights laws, not least the ECHR, help ordinary people hold the state accountable for its costliest failings.

proj-syn.title: Is Another Eurozone Debt Crisis Looming?
proj-syn.description: At a time when the cost of servicing sovereign debt is rising globally, France stands out as an especially fragile case. Its public debt-to-GDP ratio is edging up toward that of Greece on the eve of its sovereign-debt crisis, and the French political system seems unable to do anything about it.

proj-syn.title: Will AI Reverse the Renminbi’s Rise?
proj-syn.description: In China, AI-driven productivity gains will most likely be in non-tradable services, which could push down relative prices and put downward pressure on the renminbi’s real exchange rate. To ensure that this does not also mean lower income and weaker demand, policymakers should ensure that the productivity dividend is broadly shared.

proj-syn.title: The Price of You
proj-syn.description: As more people shop online, firms are increasingly setting individualized prices based on personal data, including purchase history, location, demographics, behavior, and biometric data. AI threatens to turbocharge such surveillance pricing, further widening the gap between privacy expectations and reality.

proj-syn.title: Investing in Brain Health
proj-syn.description: Just as AI agents are mastering complex cognitive tasks, our own ability to perform the same tasks is eroding. Whether AI vindicates its boosters or fizzles out like the Metaverse craze of 2022, we will not fare well without a civilization-wide effort to rebuild the cognitive skills that make technological progress possible.

proj-syn.title: Europe Still Needs Molecules
proj-syn.description: Not even the most effective European electrification strategy will eliminate the need for the molecules that fossil fuels provide. Given this, Europe must diversify its oil and gas supplies, maintain its refining capacity, and lock in decarbonization by building a hydrogen-energy industry at scale.
